summary: The Redis-backed ingestion queue remained above the 50-job alert threshold for more than three minutes.
evidence_source: simulated Prometheus incident data; not live-cluster evidence

top_hypotheses.hypothesis: The ingestion worker was saturated and could not drain jobs as quickly as they were enqueued.
Embedding-provider failures caused worker retries, reducing effective throughput.

ruled_out.reason: Queue depth increased from the normal four pending jobs to 147.
Worker CPU was near one core while the pending queue stayed above the alert threshold.

recommended_actions: Inspect ingestion-worker logs for provider errors, retries, and invalid-document failures using document IDs only.
Verify Redis connectivity and pending-job age before scaling workers.
Increase ingestion-worker replicas within the approved capacity plan after confirming the provider is healthy.
Reprocess only failed documents through the existing idempotent pipeline after the backlog is drained.
